name: Descendents
label: SST
lede: A teenage fisherman, a 34-year-old bassist headed for the post office and a shy biology student in glasses built pop-punk's blueprint in a South Bay rehearsal room, then kept pausing it for graduate school.

eras.title: Two acoustic guitars in Manhattan Beach
eras.text: Descendents began as Frank Navetta's idea and not as a hardcore band at all: surf-pop songs on acoustic guitars in the South Bay. The pieces that mattered arrived fast, a teenage drummer who fished for a living and a bassist twice his age.

years.h: Frank Navetta and David Nolte start The Itch
years.p: They write songs on acoustic guitars in Manhattan Beach, California. Navetta soon renames the project Descendents; by year's end Nolte leaves to play in The Last with his brothers.

years.h: [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] takes the drum stool
years.p: Navetta restarts Descendents with Stevenson and David Nolte, now on bass. Stevenson, still in his early teens, works as a fisherman for [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]]'s father.

years.h: Tony Lombardo, 34, joins a band of teenagers
years.p: [[Tony Lombardo|8382eec0-45d1-4b71-a5d1-1378cee856ab]] takes over the bass from Nolte. Navetta and Stevenson are both in their mid-teens.
years.xp:
Stevenson later said Lombardo looked and acted young for his age. Lombardo went to work at the U.S. Postal Service around 1982 and stayed until he retired in 2005.

The trio rehearsed in Long Beach, at the corner of 9th and Walnut. The band put that address on an album 42 years later.

eras.title: The class nerd becomes the logo
eras.text: A shy Mira Costa High kid named Milo Aukerman took the mic, and the band sped up into hardcore without losing its love songs. By the time the debut album came out, the singer on its cover was already packing for college.

years.h: A first single, on the band's own label, Orca
years.p: Cut at Media Art. Frank Navetta sings Ride the Wild; Tony Lombardo sings It's a Hectic World.
play: Ride the Wild / It's a Hectic World

years.h: Cecilia Loera sings for six months, then Milo Aukerman gets the job
years.p: Aukerman, a Mira Costa High schoolmate of Bill Stevenson's, becomes the singer after Loera's trial run.

years.h: Most of the Fat EP is over before a minute is up
years.p: The EP puts the band in the middle of the Southern California hardcore scene.

years.h: Stevenson drums for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] while Robo is stuck in England
years.p: He tries to keep both bands going; Black Flag's schedule won't allow it.
years.xp: Stevenson stayed in Black Flag until 1985 and drummed on My War, Slip It In and Loose Nut, among others, all on [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST.

years.h: Milo Goes to College, and Milo does
years.p: Recorded in June at Total Access in Redondo Beach with [[Spot|d95a08a1-80f5-4232-bdb7-4777c369f0f9]] and released on [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] and [[D. Boon|ae1757eb-8679-4cb3-8d3a-33160c953505]]'s New Alliance label, as Aukerman headed off to study biology.
years.xp:
The cover caricature is by Jeff "Rat" Atkinson, drawn from earlier cartoons by classmate Roger Deuerlein, who had cast Aukerman as the class nerd. Stevenson picked the version with the necktie for its collegiate look.

Stevenson wrote Myage on a bass he found in a trash bin. Suburban Home is Lombardo's song about wanting a normal house and a normal life. Blink-182, Sublime and Taking Back Sunday have all covered songs from the record.

years.h: Ray Cooper covers for Aukerman while he's in class
years.p: Aukerman is at El Camino College and then UC San Diego. [[Ray Cooper|cc1272fe-3cdf-46be-92c1-2eb950473991]] sings when he can't make it, and later moves to rhythm guitar.

eras.title: The band burns down, then tours itself back up
eras.text: With Stevenson drumming for Black Flag, the original band split over touring, and Navetta walked out by setting his gear on fire. Descendents came back with a new Utah rhythm section, a one-word philosophy from a fishing trip and a singer who kept leaving for the lab.

years.h: Frank Navetta sets his gear on fire and leaves for Oregon
years.p: The fight was over touring. Stevenson wanted to; Navetta and Lombardo didn't.
years.xp: Lombardo recalled it this way: "Frank said no, and I had to say no also, so he said he had to leave the band." After burning all his musical equipment, Navetta moved to Oregon and fished full time.

years.h: Without Stevenson, Cooper and Lombardo become the Ascendents
years.p: While Descendents are on hiatus and Stevenson tours with Black Flag, the two keep a band going under a name one letter off.
years.xp: It didn't last. Navetta's Wikipedia page has him in on it too, and Lombardo remembered a single show: "Frank played in his underwear... It was all a disaster."

years.h: The band regroups to record I Don't Want to Grow Up
years.p: Aukerman, Stevenson, Cooper and Lombardo record at Music Lab in Hollywood for New Alliance. [[Mark Hoppus|fcb45d6d-bf32-4c92-8211-c47f6ed3ce75]] later called Silly Girl the first song that really altered his life.
play: I Don't Want to Grow Up

years.h: Doug Carrion takes the bass when Tony Lombardo stays home
years.p: That was Lombardo on turning down the U.S. tour. He had just bought a house, was engaged and had three years in at the post office; [[Doug Carrion|bdc25394-8356-4bcd-9118-520f17af9333]] got the job.

years.h: Enjoy! comes with real farts and a Beach Boys cover
years.p: Cut in March and April at Radio Tokyo in Venice with Stevenson producing. Cooper draws the toilet-roll cover as "Scoob Droolins."
years.xp:
The song titles on the back were swapped for poop euphemisms like floater, sausage and loaf. When SST reissued it, it added Orgofart, which is exactly what it sounds like.

Reviews were mixed: AllMusic's Jeremy Salmon disliked the toilet humor but praised Kids, Wendy and Sour Grapes. Kids got the band's first music video.

years.h: The Enjoy! tour runs 58 shows in 56 cities
years.p: It covers 34 states and three Canadian provinces. When it ends, Carrion and Cooper both quit.
years.xp: Carrion said the split was friendly: he wanted to keep experimenting while the band steered another way.

years.h: Stephen Egerton and Karl Alvarez arrive from Utah
years.p: Guitarist [[Stephen Egerton|2d72eb67-f40a-4fb0-af56-4187a0d30bd5]] and bassist [[Karl Alvarez|805d18ca-2f22-4e3d-8bcd-3655ead25c31]] come from the Salt Lake City band Massacre Guys. They are still the Descendents' guitarist and bassist today.

years.h: SST buys Mike Watt's label and inherits the Descendents
years.p: [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]]'s New Alliance goes to SST, which reissues Milo Goes to College and Enjoy! on LP, cassette and CD.

years.h: All arrives with a title track that lasts one second
years.p: Recorded in January at Radio Tokyo. The song No, All! runs two seconds; Stevenson and his friend Pat McCuistion wrote both to sum up their idea of All.
years.xp: Stevenson and McCuistion came up with All on a 1980 fishing trip: the total extent, never settling for some. [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]] of Black Flag sings backing vocals. Two tours followed, recorded for Liveage! (1987) and Hallraker: Live! (1989).

years.h: Aukerman quits for graduate school after two tours
years.p: Stevenson later said he had toured Milo to death.

years.h: A fishing boat sinks with Pat McCuistion aboard
years.p: McCuistion, who co-wrote All with Stevenson, dies when the boat goes down in a storm carrying 15,000 pounds of fish. Stevenson called him the band's fifth member.

eras.title: Everybody else becomes ALL
eras.text: Without Aukerman, Stevenson, Egerton and Alvarez didn't hire a new Descendents singer. They renamed the band after its own philosophy and kept going for the next eight years.

years.big: "Let the Descendents be my and Milo's sacred thing."
years.h: The Descendents name stays shelved while ALL takes over
years.p: Stevenson, Egerton and Alvarez carry on as [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]], first with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] singer [[Dave Smalley|c637a12d-5f55-4b83-bef0-a56b3c1e326c]], later Scott Reynolds and Chad Price. The line above is Stevenson on why they didn't keep the name.
years.xp: Karl Alvarez drew ALL a mascot, Allroy, to fill the Milo cartoon's shoes. Stevenson kept the two bands separate out of respect for Aukerman's years in the Descendents.

years.h: Milo Aukerman wants back in, and nobody leaves ALL
years.p: He says he wants to make music again, so the band runs both at once: Descendents with Aukerman, ALL with Chad Price.
years.xp: Stevenson's line on it: "It's not really a reunion, we've been together the whole time." The plan made room for Aukerman without pushing Price out.

eras.title: Epitaph signs them, and the first trio plays again
eras.text: The comeback landed right as the bands Descendents inspired were selling millions. Two punk labels run by fans, Epitaph and Fat Wreck Chords, let the band record only when it wanted.

yt: When I Get Old, official video
years.h: Navetta and Lombardo come back for Everything Sucks
years.p: Recorded at Stevenson's Blasting Room in Fort Collins. Navetta writes and plays Doghouse; Lombardo plays on Eunuch Boy, the first song Aukerman ever wrote.
years.xp:
It was the band's first record to chart: No. 132 on the Billboard 200 and No. 4 on Top Heatseekers. Videos for I'm the One and When I Get Old ran as European singles.

Epitaph's [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] signed Descendents and ALL at once and let them make records whenever they chose. The tour ran almost a year, with Bouncing Souls, [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]] and [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] among the bands on the bills.

years.h: The original trio shares a stage at Stevenson's Stockage fest
years.p: Navetta, Lombardo and Stevenson play together at Stockage in Fort Collins, and record songs from 1977-81 that stay in the can for 19 years.

years.h: Eight years of silence end with Cool to Be You
years.p: Out on Fat Wreck Chords. Stevenson blamed the gap on kids and his father's death; he wrote One More Day about caring for the father he'd long been estranged from.
years.xp:
The 'Merican EP came first, in February. Fat Mike's enthusiasm helped land the band on the label; Stevenson's take on a label owner wanting to put out "probably his favorite band of all time" was "that's rad." Chris Shary drew the Milo cartoon on graph paper for the cover.

The album reached No. 143 on the Billboard 200 and No. 6 among independent albums.

eras.title: Milo's pink slip and a hit record
eras.text: The band's middle-aged years kept getting interrupted, and it kept coming back louder. A brain tumor explained Stevenson's lost years, Aukerman got laid off into full-time punk, and the band posted its highest chart spot more than 30 years in.

years.h: Frank Navetta dies on Halloween, aged 46
years.p: He had been ill for several days. Stevenson said he died in his sleep of a diabetic coma.
years.xp: Stevenson said Navetta had been in decline for years: "Frank was in very poor health. Maybe the last ten years of his life, I saw a real decline."

years.h: Stevenson has a brain tumor removed, and the band plays again
years.p: The tumor had been growing since around 2008 and draining his motivation. The same year, Descendents return for a run of shows.
years.xp: Aukerman called the shows one-offs, fit into vacation time from his biochemistry job, not a real reformation.

years.h: Filmage premieres in Toronto
years.p: Deedle LaCour and Matt Riggle's documentary on Descendents and ALL premieres at the Bloor Hot Docs cinema during NXNE, with [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], Watt and [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] among 40-plus interviews.
years.xp: The film talks to every past and present member of both bands except two: Navetta, who died in 2008, and Cooper, who declined (archival footage stands in). It went to digital on September 30, 2014 and to DVD and Blu-ray on December 2, with a 50-minute bonus cut.

yt: Milo Goes to College in full, Riot Fest Denver 2014
years.h: Tony Lombardo is back on stage at Riot Fest
years.p: Thirty years after turning down the U.S. tour, Lombardo joins the Descendents for their Riot Fest sets.

years.cap: Milo Aukerman at Southside Festival, Germany, June 2019
years.h: Laid off by DuPont, Aukerman becomes a full-time Descendent
years.p: He says he's burned out on biochemistry, the work he first left the band for in 1987.

years.h: Thirty-four years after the first LP, a No. 20 album
years.p: Hypercaffium Spazzinate is the band's highest Billboard 200 peak. [[Karl Alvarez|805d18ca-2f22-4e3d-8bcd-3655ead25c31]] wrote Feel This after his mother died.
years.xp:
It also hit No. 1 on the Independent Albums chart and No. 2 on Top Alternative Albums. The first single, Victim of Me, premiered on April 20, 2016 at a Hermosa Beach show with four other unreleased songs.

In the UK the title drew pushback over the word spaz: Real Gone called for a boycott and the charity Stay Up Late asked for a different title in Europe. A San Diego brewery later released a Descendents IPA named after a track on the record.

years.h: The 2002 tapes wait 19 years for a singer
years.p: Named for the Long Beach corner of the first rehearsal room, 9th & Walnut sets songs written in 1977-80 against tracks cut by Navetta, Lombardo and Stevenson in 2002. Aukerman sings them at home in Delaware during the pandemic.
years.xp: Eighteen tracks in 25 minutes, including a Dave Clark Five cover, and the first record with the original four since Everything Sucks. It peaked at No. 173 on the Billboard 200 and No. 12 in Germany.

years.cap: Descendents on the Canadian tour, Halifax, August 2025
years.h: A mild heart attack sidelines Milo Aukerman
years.p: Aukerman has surgery, and five European dates, Barcelona to Leicester, are canceled. The band says he's expected to fully recover.
